sections.h2: A painting contractor next door to Archer
body: Our home base is Newberry, so Archer is a short drive down the road rather than a far corner of the service area. We are a locally owned, licensed, bonded, and fully insured painting contractor in Archer, FL, with more than 15 years of painting experience and our own crews on every job. Nobody hands your house off to a subcontractor after the contract is signed.

Archer is a small rural community west of Gainesville, and its properties look the part: farmhouses set back from the road, ranch-style homes on acreage, and a few historic commercial buildings downtown. That mix calls for a painter equally comfortable on a tall farmhouse gable and a masonry storefront.

sections.h2: What we see on Archer homes and buildings
body: Most of our Archer calls come from three directions. In Downtown Archer, the older commercial buildings carry masonry, stucco, and wood trim that have been painted many times, so the work starts with finding out which layers are still bonded. In Holly Hills and Archer Estates, we tend to see ranch homes with long rooflines, deep eaves, and fascia that takes the brunt of gutter overflow. On the farm and ranch properties in between, it is lap siding, porches, outbuildings, and board fencing.

Each of those wants a different system. Wood siding and trim get 100% acrylic. Masonry and stucco with hairline movement get elastomeric. Bare or weathered wood that should look like wood gets a penetrating stain instead of a film-forming paint.

sections.h2: Open-country exposure and what it does to paint
body: A house in a subdivision is shaded by its neighbors. A farmhouse in an open field is not. Archer homes often take full sun on every elevation, so the south and west walls chalk and fade years before the north side does, and sandy soil splashes up the bottom courses every time it pours.

The flip side is moisture. Any face that stays damp, such as a porch ceiling, a shaded north wall, or the boards closest to irrigation, grows mildew and algae quickly in this climate. We treat mildew at the root during prep, take moisture readings on suspect wood, and replace rotted fascia or trim rather than coating over it. You can read more about the warning signs in our guide to hidden moisture behind siding.

sections.h2: How an Archer project runs from first call to final walk
body: Call or request a quote and we usually schedule the walkthrough within 48 hours. A crew lead, not a salesperson, comes out to measure, photograph conditions, and take moisture readings where they matter. The written, itemized estimate generally arrives within one business day and names the surfaces included and excluded, the prep steps, the primer and topcoat products, the number of coats, and the schedule. Nothing gets added later without your written approval.

Most projects start one to three weeks after approval. Prep days come first: washing, scraping, sanding, mildew treatment, nail pops, rot and fascia repair, re-caulking, and spot-priming. Then two full coats go on, with a third for big color changes or thirsty surfaces. A full exterior typically runs three to seven working days plus wash and dry time, and October through May is the best exterior window.
The job closes with a punch walk you sign. Anything not right gets fixed before we leave, exterior work carries a written workmanship warranty of up to 10 years, and you keep labelled touch-up paint.

faqs.q: Do you paint rural properties outside Archer's town limits?
faqs.a: Yes. Farmhouses, ranch homes, outbuildings, and fencing on acreage around Archer are a regular part of our work. The crew lead notes access, distances, and any outbuildings during the walkthrough so the estimate covers them.

faqs.q: How quickly can you come out to Archer for an estimate?
faqs.a: Walkthroughs are usually scheduled within 48 hours, and the itemized written quote typically follows within one business day. Most approved projects start one to three weeks later.

faqs.q: Are your Archer crews licensed and insured?
faqs.a: We are licensed, bonded, and fully insured in Florida, and every crew member is covered by workers' comp. Commercial and HOA clients can get a certificate of insurance naming their entity before we mobilize.

faqs.q: What paint do you use on Archer farmhouses?
faqs.a: Premium Sherwin-Williams or Benjamin Moore lines: 100% acrylic on wood siding and trim, elastomeric on stucco with hairline cracking, and penetrating stain on exposed wood. The exact product is named on your estimate.
